rawAskedItems.item: Publication date of the June 2013 NASA/JPL account
rawAskedItems.statement: June 27, 2013 — displayed on the JPL page "NASA's Voyager 1 Explores Final Frontier of Our 'Solar Bubble'" (memory-5).

rawAskedItems.item: Publication date of the September 2013 NASA account
rawAskedItems.statement: Sept. 12, 2013 — displayed on the JPL/NASA page "NASA Spacecraft Embarks on Historic Journey Into Interstellar Space" (memory-4).

rawAskedItems.item: Crossing date eventually accepted by the Voyager team
rawAskedItems.statement: August 25, 2012: "The Voyager team generally accepts this date as the date of interstellar arrival" (memory-3).

rawAskedItems.item: The missing sign behind the June 2013 'not yet' conclusion and why the team wanted it
rawAskedItems.statement: The third of three expected signs — an abrupt change in magnetic field direction indicating the interstellar magnetic field — had not been seen; field direction changed no more than 2 degrees, so the team held Voyager was still in the sun's magnetic domain (memory-1).

rawAskedItems.item: The later measurement that changed the conclusion, including what it measured
rawAskedItems.statement: Plasma density from plasma-wave oscillations excited by a March 2012 coronal mass ejection: the pitch showed plasma 40+ times denser than in the heliosphere — interstellar plasma; Voyager's plasma sensor was not working, so this was the substitute measurement (memory-3).
The CME reached Voyager 1 in April 2013, 13 months after erupting; the plasma wave instrument detected the oscillations on April 9, 2013 (memory-3, memory-2).

The plasma wave team's own archive, revealing fainter oscillations in October and November 2012; extrapolated densities from both events gave August 2012, consistent with abrupt durable energetic-particle changes first detected Aug. 25, 2012 (memory-3).

rawAskedItems.item: Why this was not simply a crossing between the two announcements
rawAskedItems.statement: Voyager had already crossed on Aug. 25, 2012 — before the June 27, 2013 release. The June 'not yet' conclusion rested on a missing expected sign (field direction) and pre-April-9 data; what changed by Sept. 12 was the evidence (new density measurement plus reinterpretation of 2012 data), not the spacecraft's location (memory-1, memory-3).
